description: Worktree node_modules — symlink from main repo ONLY if the branch doesn't touch packages/*; otherwise full `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` in the worktree
metadata:

Git worktrees under `.claude/worktrees/` start with **no `node_modules`** — checks fail with `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND: @repo/eslint-config` because this is a pnpm workspace and `@repo/*` packages live in per-package `node_modules`.

**Why (updated 2026-07-10, ENG-2019):** Symlinks resolve `@repo/*` workspace packages to the MAIN repo's checkout. That's only correct when the worktree branch leaves `packages/*` untouched. If the branch adds/changes anything in `packages/*`, tsc/eslint see the stale main-repo copy; and MIXED states (some dirs symlinked, some real from a filtered install) are worst of all — one mix broke Roam's global types, another broke Obsidian's React 18/19 peer resolution.

**How to apply:**
- Branch touches only `apps/*` code: symlink root + per-package `node_modules` from the main repo (fast, gitignored, never committed).
- Branch touches `packages/*`: run `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` at the worktree root instead (shared pnpm store, ~5–45s). If a mixed symlink/real state exists, remove the symlinks and `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --force` to rebuild the virtual store cleanly.
- Never run `--no-frozen-lockfile` casually: it re-resolves unrelated packages (an @types/node dedup cascaded into React type mixing that broke Obsidian tsc, would have been red CI). To add one dep, hand-add the importer entry to pnpm-lock.yaml reusing an existing catalog resolution (PR #1216 did it in 3 lines), then frozen install.

**Root `pnpm ci:validate` in a symlinked worktree (2026-09-02, ENG-2141):** symlink EVERY workspace that has a package.json, not just the ones you touch. `apps/tldraw-sync-worker/node_modules` was missing and turbo failed fast on its `check-types`, skipping every other task. Separately, the main checkout's virtual-store hoist `node_modules/.pnpm/node_modules/@types/react` was a July link to React 18 types while packages/ui needs 19, so `@repo/ui check-types` failed locally even though `.pnpm/lock.yaml` matched the lockfile and CI at the same commit was green. That is a main-checkout environment problem (a fresh frozen install there), not something to fix from a worktree. Fallback proof when it bites: `pnpm exec turbo run test:unit` at the worktree root plus per-app `tsc`, and cite the green CI run at the base SHA.

**Husky rewrites the shared hooks path (2026-09-25):** `pnpm install` in a worktree runs the root `prepare` script (`husky`), which sets the repo-wide `core.hooksPath` to relative `.husky/_`. The main checkout's value is absolute `/mnt/data/projects/discourse-graph/.husky/_` (the Entire hook wrappers live there). After any worktree install, check `git config core.hooksPath` and restore the absolute value if it changed.

See [[feedback_stay_in_worktree]], [[feedback_rename_worktree_branch_before_push]], [[feedback_fix_relocated_lint_warnings]].

name: feedback-stay-in-worktree
description: "When the session env says the working dir is a git worktree, never cd to the main repo path — Bash cwd persists, and absolute Edit paths will silently target the wrong checkout"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 66a59f46-b22d-467a-93d6-1726749382d8

When the session environment header says `Primary working directory: /mnt/data/projects/discourse-graph/.claude/worktrees/<TICKET>`, do not `cd` out of that worktree for ANY command — not for lint, not for tsc, not for grep, not for anything.

**Why:** The Bash tool's cwd persists between commands. The moment I run `cd /mnt/data/projects/discourse-graph/apps/roam && npx eslint ...`, every subsequent `Edit` with an absolute path under `/mnt/data/projects/discourse-graph/apps/roam/...` lands in the main repo on `main`, not the worktree. The Edit tool happily writes the file because the path exists — there is no warning. By the time I notice (often only when the user says "I don't see it in my IDE"), the main branch's working tree has half a PR's worth of uncommitted changes, and the worktree is empty.

This happened once on ENG-1660: 5 files edited in main on branch `main` instead of the worktree. Recovery required `git diff > patch`, `git apply` in worktree, `git restore` in main. Easy to fix but a real risk every time — if the user had run `git add -A && git commit` from main while I was still editing, my changes would land on `main` directly.

**Second failure mode (ENG-1575): a read-only `cd` poisons the build/copy/verify pipeline.** Here the Edits were fine (absolute worktree paths), but I `cd`'d to `/mnt/data/projects/discourse-graph/apps/roam` for a *harmless-feeling* read-only peek at shared `node_modules` (Blueprint source) and never cd'd back. The next `npm run build`, `npx eslint/tsc`, and `cp dist/.` all inherited main as cwd — so I built `main` (none of the PR's commits), copied that to the test dir, and the "passing" lint/tsc validated main's unedited file. I shipped a wrong build to the user's test dir and reported it as correct. The read-only cd is the sneaky one: it doesn't trip the Edit-path check, so nothing feels wrong until the artifact is already out. **Detection cue:** print `pwd` + `git rev-parse --short HEAD` at the top of any build/check command — if HEAD isn't the worktree branch's tip, cwd has drifted.

**How to apply:**
- Use absolute paths starting with the worktree path: `/mnt/data/projects/discourse-graph/.claude/worktrees/<TICKET>/apps/roam/...`.
- For Bash commands that have a working-directory requirement (lint, prettier, tsc, pnpm scripts), use `git -C <worktree>` or run from the worktree path: `(cd /mnt/data/projects/discourse-graph/.claude/worktrees/<TICKET>/apps/roam && npx eslint ...)` so the subshell exits without changing the parent cwd.
- Or use `pushd`/`popd` style: `cd /path/to/worktree/apps/roam && ... && cd -`.

# PR guidelines

This is the repository source for the DevOps PR process. Code standards live in [STYLE_GUIDE.md](STYLE_GUIDE.md); agent instructions live in [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md). Production changes, releases, and work intake remain in DevOps.

## Scope and structure

- Use one PR per Linear ticket. You may batch very minor, unrelated changes of a few lines when they are low risk.
- Scope the ticket to one specific problem. If additional problems need attention, pause that additional work and check with the team or lead before implementing it.
- Use separate PRs for unrelated refactors, feature additions, dependency updates, and lint or style fixes. Keep scope to a single package or app when possible.
- For features spanning packages, make foundational changes such as types and shared utilities first, then use separate PRs for usage and integration.

## Size and review guidance

About 200 added plus removed lines is a useful target. Up to 400 lines is acceptable when the change is scoped and self-contained. Ideally, touch fewer than five files; repetitive mechanical changes can justify more. These are review guidelines, not automatic rejection thresholds.

Test changes do not count toward the 400-line threshold.

Above 400 changed lines, explain why the PR cannot reasonably be split. Include the main review entry points and intended testing path in Reviewer brief. Keep this concise rather than adding a file-by-file summary.

## Branches and PR metadata

- Use Linear's generated branch name through Copy Branch Name.
- For Linear-backed work, use `ENG-#### Exact Linear ticket title` as the PR title. This is the repository convention in place of the alternative title formats previously listed in DevOps.

- Run `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, then `pnpm ci:validate` from the repository root before opening a PR or declaring it ready. Resolve failures before requesting review. A draft must disclose unresolved validation blockers.

## Mode gate (run FIRST, before Step 0)

Decide which mode this run needs. This is a judgment call you make from evidence — not a rule to apply mechanically, and not something to take on faith from the dispatching prompt (dispatch prompts are written fresh each run and can get this wrong in either direction):
- Evidence a full pass already ran on this PR: a previous run's line-anchored annotations posted on the PR, existing review threads answering a prior findings report, or the dispatcher naming a last-reviewed SHA.

If you judge that, run full and say why.

## Step 0 — Inventory

The change set is the FULL PR diff: `git diff <base>...HEAD` (merge-base three-dot against the PR's base branch — the stack parent for stacked PRs, else main) plus staged/unstaged changes. Never review only the latest commits: reviewers see the whole PR, and code that landed on the branch before this run is still your surface. (Exception: Re-review mode below.) Classify changed files:
- **DATA**: `packages/database/**`, `*.sql`, any file containing a Supabase/PostgREST call (`.from(`), datalog query, or cross-app contract type
- **FRONTEND**: `apps/roam/**`, `apps/obsidian/**`, `apps/website/**` UI code
- **OTHER**: tests, docs, config

Steps 2 and 3 are scoped: skip the data-layer pass if no DATA files changed; skip the frontend pass if no FRONTEND files changed. Never skip steps 1 and 4.

1c. **Literal hoist.** Repeated or typo-prone string literals (prop keys, selectors, attribute names, ids) appearing more than once or shared with other files → must be a named constant defined once.

245	## Mode gate (run FIRST, before Step 0)
246	
247	Decide which mode this run needs. This is a judgment call you make from evidence — not a rule to apply mechanically, and not something to take on faith from the dispatching prompt (dispatch prompts are written fresh each run and can get this wrong in either direction):
248	- Evidence a full pass already ran on this PR: a previous run's line-anchored annotations posted on the PR, existing review threads answering a prior findings report, or the dispatcher naming a last-reviewed SHA.
249	- Default when a full pass ran and the commits since only answer review feedback: Re-review mode below.

251	- The first line of your output states the chosen mode and the reasoning — that's what keeps the choice reviewable, whichever way it goes.
252	
253	## Step 0 — Inventory
254	
255	The change set is the FULL PR diff: `git diff <base>...HEAD` (merge-base three-dot against the PR's base branch — the stack parent for stacked PRs, else main) plus staged/unstaged changes. 256	- **DATA**: `packages/database/**`, `*.sql`, any file containing a Supabase/PostgREST call (`.from(`), datalog query, or cross-app contract type
257	- **FRONTEND**: `apps/roam/**`, `apps/obsidian/**`, `apps/website/**` UI code
258	- **OTHER**: tests, docs, config
259	
260	Steps 2 and 3 are scoped: skip the data-layer pass if no DATA files changed; skip the frontend pass if no FRONTEND files changed. Never skip steps 1 and 4.
261	
262	## Re-review mode (follow-up pushes)
263	
264	If a full pre-pr-review already ran on this PR and this run covers a follow-up push (fixes after a review round or a previous run's findings), do NOT repeat the full sequence:

266	- Change set = `git diff <last-reviewed-sha>...HEAD` — the commits since the state the previous round covered, not the whole PR again.

273	
274	1a. **Reuse gate.** List every NEW named thing in the diff (function, type, component, constant, enum, marker string). ## Dependencies
There's no hard dependency, so all six start now in parallel. Three tickets touch shared code, though:

1. **ENG-2195 and ENG-2351** both edit `mapNodeTypeIdToLocal` in `apps/obsidian/src/utils/importNodes.ts`. ENG-2195 owns the `format` derivation in `parseSchemaLiteralContent`. ENG-2351 owns the template block below it. Both can reuse helpers that already exist (`checkInvalidChars`, `sanitizeFileName`, `createTemplateFileWithUniqueName`), so neither needs a new shared helper. Whichever merges second rebases one hunk.
2. **ENG-2348 and your draft #1479 (ENG-2296)** both edit `DiscoverSharedNodesDialog.tsx`, the import entry point. Default: ENG-2348 branches from `main` and adds the warning as a self-contained component rendered by one line, so the rebase stays small. Tell me if you'd rather stack it on `eng-2296`.
3. **ENG-2195 vs ENG-2176:** Michael flagged these as possible duplicates. They aren't. ENG-2195 makes imported formats safe to use as filenames at import time. ENG-2176 makes the format-to-regex builder escape metacharacters in both apps. They don't share any files.

| Ticket | Area | Main entry points |
|---|---|---|
| ENG-2176 | Roam, Obsidian and a shared package (largest; Post v0) | both `getDiscourseNodeFormatExpression` / `extractContentFromTitle` copies, `DiscourseContextView`, `QueryEngine`, `matchDiscourseNode` |
| ENG-2195 | Obsidian | `importNodes.ts`, `validateNodeType.ts` |
| ENG-2348 | Roam | the share dialog and `DiscoverSharedNodesDialog` (a warning, not a block, per the ticket's Solution) |
| ENG-2349 | Roam UI | `TentativeRelationInstances.tsx` (`roam-global-tailwind`) |
| ENG-2350 | Roam | `resolveSharedNodeTypes.ts` and the settings accessors |
| ENG-2351 | Obsidian | `importNodes.ts`, `templates.ts`; first confirm Roam really sends the template without a title |

## Workflow for each ticket
1. **Implementer agent** (Opus, one per worktree):
   - Treats the ticket as the spec and the code as the source of truth, and adds tests.
   - Runs eslint, prettier and tsc, then `pnpm ci:validate` and the app build.
   - Reads the full diff against `STYLE_GUIDE.md`.
   - Commits one worktree at a time behind a lock, with no Co-Authored-By line.
   - Pushes and opens a draft PR from the template, with Loom marked "Pending".
2. **Independent review agent** for each PR runs `/pre-pr-review` (this covers the delegated full-review checkbox), `scope-check` and `dg-pr-adherence-check`. I decide what to act on, the implementer fixes it, and follow-up pushes get re-reviewed. Bot comments get fixed or answered.
3. **Where each one stops:** draft PR open, checks green, review findings closed, Loom pending. Nobody launches Roam. Each PR comes with a live-check runbook for you, and the videos happen in a separate session.

If an agent hits a question the ticket and code don't answer, it picks a default, records it and keeps going. I'll batch those for you. Questions that would change the approach come to you before any code is written.

**Yours to answer:** on ENG-2195, Michael asked why you removed yourself as assignee, and pinged again today. None of the six tickets has an assignee, and I'm not changing that.

## The ticket (verbatim; this is the spec)

### Problem
* `getDiscourseNodeFormatExpression` (same logic in `apps/obsidian/src/utils/getDiscourseNodeFormatExpression.ts` and `apps/roam/src/utils/getDiscourseNodeFormatExpression.ts`) escapes only `[ ] ? . +` before substituting `{placeholder}` with `(.*?)`. A format containing any other metacharacter — `( ) * ^ $ |` — builds a regex that never matches its own titles: `Claim (draft) - {content}` compiles to `^Claim (draft) - (.*?)$`, which requires the literal title `Claim draft …` and turns `(draft)` into a capture group. Source: Codex P2 on #1318 (https://github.com/DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph/pull/1318#discussion_r3815409797).
* Consequences by call site:
  * Obsidian `extractContentFromTitle` (ENG-2154/#1318): no match → `core_title` falls back to the full decorated basename — a non-null wrong value that null-probe backfills (ENG-2155-style) skip.
  * A literal `(…)` group also breaks the placeholder↔capture-group 1:1 invariant that the positional `{content}` lookups in both #1318 and #1317 rely on — though misextraction needs the mangled regex to still match a real title (an alternation or an aligned stray group), so the dominant failure in practice is the no-match fallback above.
  * Obsidian QueryEngine (×2), `createNode`, `DiscourseContextView`, and Roam `matchDiscourseNode`: metachar formats silently never match, so those nodes are invisible to format matching.

### Solution
* Escape every regex metacharacter in the literal portions of the format while leaving `{[a-zA-Z]+}` placeholders intact (substitute placeholders first or split on them, then escape the literal segments — a blanket escape would also escape the braces and break substitution).
* Fix both apps in one PR: the builders must stay identical or `core_title` semantics diverge cross-app.
* Preferred shape: hoist `getDiscourseNodeFormatExpression` + `extractContentFromTitle` into a shared package (pure cross-app text transforms belong there, and a package has a vitest runner that apps/obsidian lacks), replacing the per-app copies, the divergent inline copy in `DiscourseContextView.tsx` (which can render a different Content string than the published `core_title`), and Roam's wider `{[\w\d-]+}` placeholder scan (#1317) that mismatches its builder. One grammar, one implementation, tested. Per-app grammar constants are the fallback if the hoist is blocked.

### Done When
* `Claim (draft) - {content}` matches its titles and extracts `content` in both apps.
* One shared, unit-tested implementation of builder + extractor (at minimum: scan and builder share one grammar constant per app), and `DiscourseContextView` renders the same content string the converter publishes.
* Formats without metacharacters behave identically to today.

### Out of Scope
* Value-aware repair of `core_title` rows already written with the fallback value (same follow-up story as ENG-2155's wrong-value pass).

### Notes
* Deferred from #1318 because the builder has five Obsidian call sites plus the Roam matchers — matching behavior changes everywhere, so it needs its own PR and test pass.

Ticket comments: Michael Gartner flagged ENG-2195 ("Normalize imported node type formats for Obsidian filenames") as a possible duplicate. It is not: ENG-2195 normalizes imported formats for filename safety at the Obsidian schema-import boundary and is being implemented by a sibling agent right now. Do not touch `apps/obsidian/src/utils/importNodes.ts`'s `parseSchemaLiteralContent`/`mapNodeTypeIdToLocal` or `validateNodeType.ts` unless a builder call site there forces it.

- Files referencing `getDiscourseNodeFormatExpression` or `extractContentFromTitle` on main:
  - Obsidian: `src/utils/conceptConversion.ts`, `src/components/DiscourseContextView.tsx`, `src/services/QueryEngine.ts`, `src/utils/extractContentFromTitle.ts`, `src/utils/createNode.ts`, `src/utils/getDiscourseNodeFormatExpression.ts`

  - Shared: `packages/database/src/lib/decorateTitle.ts` (the shared title decorator both apps already use).
- Both apps already depend on `@repo/utils` (`packages/utils/src` has `resolveSchemaFormat.ts`, `execContext.ts`, ...) and `@repo/database`. Hoisting needs no new dependency, so no `pnpm install`. Pick the package with evidence (where the related decorate logic and format helpers already live), and say why in the PR.
- Obsidian now has a vitest runner (`apps/obsidian` `pnpm test:unit`); the ticket's "apps/obsidian lacks" remark is stale, but the hoist is still the ticket's preferred shape.
